content:
maria: NLB targets for edge-service in us-west-2 are getting dropped by the load balancer — console shows 'target failed health checks'. Anyone else seeing this?
ajay: Yep, started ~08:41 UTC. About 25-35% of targets removed in the ASG. Pods report Ready though.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: edge-service v2 rolled to 40% at 08:39 UTC (canary).
maria: The timing aligns with the canary rollout, but I also see a bunch of kube-proxy restarts on those nodes around the same time.
nate: grabbing host logs... seeing conntrack / NAT allocation errors on node kernel:
```
kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
kube-proxy[pid]: conntrack: err: port allocation failed
```
ajay: If kube-proxy or the CNI is restarting mid-rollout, we can get SNAT/conntrack churn. NLB health checks come in to the node port and if conntrack is busted the TCP handshake can get reset or timed out -> NLB marks unhealthy.
maria: svc is currently externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster (confirmed). That causes additional SNAT hairpinning for node -> pod forwarding.
ajay: yeah, Cluster mode plus a burst of ephemeral outbound connections during rollout can exhaust nf_conntrack. Health checks from NLB will then either time out or see RSTs.
sre-oncall: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) pause rollout 2) increase conntrack table on affected nodes 3) flush conntrack entries if safe 4) consider switching to externalTrafficPolicy: Local for edge-service canary to avoid SNAT for checks.
ops-bot: Runbook triggered: increased net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on 3 nodes and paused the rollout.
maria: Running: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=4000000` and then `conntrack -F` on nodes that are safe to restart. Doing one node at a time.
ajay: Also watch CloudWatch metrics: TargetHealth->UnhealthyHostCount and ELB-->SurgeOfReset count. If targets come back within ~2m after conntrack clear it's likely transient.
nate: After clearing conntrack on node-12 and node-14, NLB re-registered those targets in ~90s. Logs show previous healthcheck attempts saw TCP RSTs with src port 0x0 due to allocation failure.
maria: Good recovery. We'll keep rollout paused and do a controlled canary with externalTrafficPolicy: Local and smaller batch size while we validate.
ajay: Long term: 1) increase conntrack defaults in kops/launch template, 2) tune kube-proxy conntrack min/timeout, 3) avoid big simultaneous CNI/kube-proxy restarts during rollouts, 4) consider Local for services that are fronted by NLB.
sre-oncall: Filing incident ticket and scheduling postmortem. Root cause summary: SNAT/conntrack exhaustion during a service rollout + externalTrafficPolicy=Cluster led to TCP healthcheck resets -> NLB marked targets unhealthy and deregistered them.
maria: I'll update the incident ticket with steps taken and follow-up items. Paused rollout until we have a small experiment with Local mode.
ops-bot: Next actions checklist created in #incidents. @maria @ajay @nate :thumbsup:
